wiki-iran.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Iran each day. It jumps when the country is at the centre of a war, a negotiation or a crisis, so the spikes mark the days the wider world went looking for background.
wiki-iran.recent: Tehran told Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir, who is carrying mediators' proposals, that no enriched uranium will leave Iran, the sticking point in ending the US-Israeli war on Iran. Iran also offered to reopen Hormuz within 6 days, blacklisted 122 ships, and its Guards said mines set 2 tankers ablaze.

brent.standing: The price of a barrel of North Sea crude, and the reference against which most of the world's internationally traded oil is priced. Petrol, diesel and jet fuel costs follow it, and so do the budgets of oil-exporting states.
brent.recent: With Hormuz closed, Saudi Arabia's way around it was the East-West pipeline to Yanbu, and a Houthi drone strike near Saudi Aramco's Shaybah oilfield put that bypass at risk too. Iran's Guards claimed mines set 2 tankers ablaze in Hormuz, and the US ordered staff and families out of Saudi Arabia.

wti.standing: West Texas Intermediate: the price of a barrel of light, sweet crude delivered at Cushing, Oklahoma, and the benchmark for American oil. US petrol and diesel prices follow it, and so do shale drillers' budgets.
wti.recent: With mines laid in Hormuz, 12 ships were attacked near the strait in one week and missiles were fired at the Saudi route around it through Yanbu. Russian supply prospects, as Trump eased sanctions on Russian fuel, briefly pulled futures back, while shipping US crude to Asia now costs $40 a barrel, Vitol says.

natgas-hh.standing: The futures price of gas delivered at Henry Hub in Louisiana, the benchmark for the American market. It moves on weather, storage and LNG exports, and sets what US power plants and households pay for heat and electricity.
natgas-hh.recent: The fortnight's gas shocks landed abroad: with Iran holding Hormuz shut, Dutch benchmark futures passed $1,000 per 1,000 cubic metres and a Qatari tanker took the Red Sea route to Poland. Nothing in the reporting ties those events to the US contract.

wheat.standing: The export price of a tonne of US hard red winter wheat loaded at the Gulf of Mexico, a reference for bread wheat worldwide. Importers from Egypt to Indonesia buy against it, and bread subsidy budgets strain when it rises.
wheat.recent: The fortnight's stories were about where the grain goes rather than what it costs: Germany asked Russia to stop hitting civilian ships in the Black Sea, Egypt released state wheat to mills from LE16,500 a tonne, and Punjab bought 160,000 tonnes against a 2.5 million target. None of it accounts for the year's price.

rice.standing: The export price of a tonne of Thai white rice, the benchmark much of Asia's and Africa's import trade is priced against. Rice is the staple for about half the world, so a move here reaches household food budgets directly.

copper.standing: The price of a tonne of refined copper, the metal in every wire, motor and transformer. Demand follows construction and electrification, and supply rests on a handful of mines in Chile, Peru and the Congo.
copper.recent: Everything reported this fortnight postdates the latest reading: two unions struck Antofagasta's Centinela mine in Chile and reached a preliminary deal, International Resources Holding paid $620 million for 51% of Mopani in Zambia, and Mercuria advanced $250 million against Congolese copper. None of it accounts for the climb on the chart.

us-10y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for ten years, set by trading in its bonds. Mortgages, corporate loans and other governments' debt are priced off it, so it sets the cost of money well beyond America.
us-10y.recent: Traders priced 80% odds of a December Fed hike while Warsh withheld guidance, calling AI a shock to the economy, and the European Central Bank also heads for a December hike. The IMF warned emerging economies will spend almost 11% of taxes on debt. The retreat since tracks an AI chip rout that sank the Kospi and sent money into Treasuries.

sp500.standing: An index of 500 large companies listed on US stock exchanges, weighted by market value. It is the benchmark most pension and index funds are measured against, and a handful of technology firms carry much of its weight.

nasdaq100.standing: The 100 largest non-financial companies listed on the Nasdaq exchange in New York, weighted by size. A handful of technology giants make up most of it, so it reads as the price of American big tech.
nasdaq100.recent: The fortnight's company news centred on Meta: a New Mexico judge ordered it to pay $25 billion for deceiving Facebook users, and its free cash flow turned negative. None of that accounts for the index's path over the window.

us-gas-retail.standing: The average price US drivers pay for a gallon of regular gasoline at the pump, taxes included. It follows crude oil and refining costs with a lag, and it is the energy price American households and voters notice most.
us-gas-retail.recent: Gasoline drove US consumer prices up 0.6% in September, 3.7% over the year, and revived bets on a Fed hike. With oil above $110 on a war-driven shock, Trump eased sanctions on Russian fuel, and the first tanker of Russian diesel, 40,000 tonnes, heads for the US on Thursday.

natgas-ttf.standing: The wholesale price of natural gas in Europe, set at the Dutch TTF hub where the continent's pipeline and LNG supplies are traded. Household heating bills, power prices and fertiliser costs across the EU follow it.
natgas-ttf.recent: Dutch benchmark gas futures passed $1,000 per 1,000 cubic metres, the highest since 2022, as European storage sat at a record low. Qatar ramped up LNG exports and sent a cargo on a rare Red Sea journey toward Poland, while in Britain gas explains £161 of a £180 bill rise.

vix.standing: The CBOE Volatility Index: the swing in the S&P 500 over the next 30 days implied by the prices of its options. It rises when investors pay more for protection against a fall, which is why it is called the fear gauge.

fx-pkr.standing: What one US dollar costs in Pakistani rupees, under a float the State Bank of Pakistan manages. Pakistan pays for its fuel imports in dollars, so a weaker rupee reaches pump prices and household bills.
fx-pkr.recent: The fortnight brought Pakistan's suspension of trade with Iran at the Gabd-Rimdan and Taftan crossings, and a fuel-price revision that cut petrol by Rs2.71 a litre while raising diesel, but none of it accounts for the rupee's path against the dollar.

fx-ngn.standing: Nigeria's currency, quoted as naira per US dollar. Africa's most populous country earns most of its dollars from crude oil and imports much of what it consumes, so the rate sets what fuel and food cost there.
fx-ngn.recent: The fortnight's news from Nigeria was about prices at home rather than the currency. The central bank restated its single-digit inflation target with headline inflation down to about 15% from about 35%, food inflation rose to 19.59%, and Abuja moved to negotiate a petrol price ceiling. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-egp.standing: How many Egyptian pounds buy one US dollar. Egypt imports much of its wheat and fuel and owes heavily in dollars, so a weaker pound feeds straight into food prices and the cost of servicing its debt.
fx-egp.recent: The fortnight brought Egypt a Moody's upgrade as inflation eased, and a council decision to send troops to Saudi Arabia for its Houthi war, on which parliament put off its vote. None of it accounts for the pound's slide against the dollar.

fx-try.standing: How many Turkish lira buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening lira. Turkey imports most of its energy and its companies owe heavily in foreign currency, so the rate feeds straight into prices and repayments.
fx-try.recent: The fortnight's Turkish news was about defence pacts with Qatar, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, eastern Libya's backing of the 2019 maritime deal, the Sakarya gas platform and the state takeover of Halk TV, and none of it accounts for the exchange rate.

fx-bdt.standing: What one US dollar costs in Bangladeshi taka, a rate the central bank manages closely. Garment exports and remittances from workers abroad supply the dollars; fuel, cotton and food imports spend them.
fx-bdt.recent: The fortnight's news from Bangladesh centred on its workers abroad, from the fees Malaysia-bound Bangladeshis pay to the two executed in Saudi Arabia without notice to Dhaka, and on a measles outbreak at home. None of it accounts for the rate.

fx-idr.standing: How many rupiah one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker currency. Indonesia sells coal, nickel and palm oil in dollars and relies on foreign buyers for its bonds, so it moves with commodity prices and capital flows.
fx-idr.recent: MSCI moved to remove Indonesia from its global indexes, and funds that track those benchmarks had to sell: Jakarta stocks fell to a six-year low, then lost 11.6% in a single Friday, the worst day since 1998. Foreign holders converting the proceeds into dollars carried that selling from the stock market into the currency.

fx-lbp.standing: The price of one US dollar in Lebanese pounds. Lebanon imports most of its food, fuel and medicine and pays for them in dollars, so the rate sets what a salary earned in pounds can buy.
fx-lbp.recent: Lebanon's news this month was the war: Israeli attacks had killed 4,387 people, fresh strikes hit southern Lebanon, and Iran pressed for an all-front ceasefire. None of it accounts for the pound's small drift, which reflects a rate the central bank keeps pinned.

fx-cny.standing: How many Chinese yuan one US dollar buys. The central bank sets a daily reference rate and lets trading stray only 2% either side, so the rate is partly policy, and it decides how cheap Chinese exports are abroad.
fx-cny.recent: The fortnight brought work on the yuan's plumbing rather than its price: Hong Kong recruited foreign banks into its Central Moneymarkets Unit to deepen offshore yuan clearing, and China's central bank said it would lend to funds, not just banks. Neither accounts for the yuan's firming.

fx-inr.standing: How many rupees buy one US dollar, so a rising line is a weakening rupee. The Reserve Bank of India manages it loosely, and because India imports most of its oil, a weaker rupee raises fuel prices for 1.4 billion people.
fx-inr.recent: The rupee's recovery followed India's first repo rate rise since 2023, to 5.5%, with further hikes signalled as inflation risks mount. A higher rate makes holding rupees pay more. Then in Mumbai, Rubio tied India's Russian oil waiver to its trade deal with Washington, opening the way to a reset with India's largest export market.

fx-brl.standing: How many Brazilian reais one US dollar buys; a higher number is a weaker real. Brazil exports soy, iron ore and oil and pays high interest rates, so the currency moves on commodity prices and on doubts about public spending.
fx-brl.recent: The fortnight was dominated by the runoff between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, with polls narrowing from a Bolsonaro lead to a tie, and his potential finance chief promising a fast fiscal policy fix. Nothing reported links that race to the real, whose firming came early in October, before most of those polls.

fx-mxn.standing: The number of Mexican pesos one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker peso. Latin America's most traded currency, it moves on US trade policy and interest rates, because most of Mexico's exports go north.
fx-mxn.recent: Mexico's own news in the period was corporate and criminal: AT&T sold its 24.7 million Mexican subscribers for $2 billion, Mexico City gave Meta, TikTok and X a month to protect minors, and a prison fight in Mazatlán killed 10. None of it accounts for the peso's slide against the dollar.

fx-eur.standing: How many euros one US dollar buys. The euro is shared by most European Union states and is the world's second reserve currency; it moves on the gap between ECB and Federal Reserve interest rates.
fx-eur.recent: The euro lost ground as Dutch benchmark gas futures topped $1,000 per 1,000 cubic metres with storage at a record low, an import bill paid in dollars. France's protests became a political crisis and its 10-year yield hit 4.96%, highest since 2002, outweighing an ECB headed for a December hike.

fx-jpy.standing: How many yen one US dollar buys, so a rising line is a weaker yen. Japan pays for nearly all its energy in dollars, and its low interest rates have long made the yen the currency the world borrows cheaply.
fx-jpy.recent: Yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago, as the Iran war lifted energy costs and a weak yen compounded them. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama says inflation is turning wage-driven, a case for raising the Bank of Japan's 1.25% rate, already a 31-year high, even as Tokyo cuts the consumption tax to cushion households.

fx-rub.standing: How many rubles buy one US dollar. Russia earns its foreign currency mostly from oil and gas, and sanctions and capital controls shape the rate, so it moves on energy prices and state policy as much as on trade.
fx-rub.recent: The ruble firmed as Russia's exports fetched more and met fewer barriers: Brent sat above $109 over Hormuz, Trump put on hold the Russia sanctions he signed into law, and 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel headed for the US. Witkoff's Moscow visit ended with the Kremlin ready to resume Ukraine talks by mid-November.

fx-zar.standing: South Africa's currency, quoted as rand per US dollar, so a rising line means a weaker rand. One of the most traded emerging-market currencies, it moves with the metals the country exports and with global appetite for risk.
fx-zar.recent: South Africa's fortnight brought a fuel levy cut running until January 2027, riots in Durban and Soweto that forced the withdrawal of an asylum directive, and Navi Pillay's Nobel Peace Prize, but none of it accounts for the currency's moves.

btc.standing: The dollar price of one bitcoin, the first and largest cryptocurrency, whose supply is capped at 21 million coins. It trades around the clock, and the rest of the crypto market tends to move with it.
btc.recent: Bitcoin moved with tech shares this week. It rallied on the AI-earnings rebound and on SpaceX and Tesla exploring a merger holding 30,000 BTC, as ETFs took in $1 billion in 3 days, then gave it back when Tesla and Meta failed to calm AI nerves. Separately, MSCI rules threaten to eject bitcoin treasury firms such as Strategy.

eth.standing: The token of the Ethereum network, the blockchain most stablecoins, lending protocols and tokenised assets run on. Every transaction there is paid for in it, so its price tracks use of the network as well as appetite for crypto.
eth.recent: Nothing in the fortnight's reporting explains ether's slide. In the same weeks, crypto traders lost $51.6 million on chip-stock perpetual futures over one weekend, Hacken counted $1.18 billion stolen across 107 incidents in Q3, and Bitcoin climbed back above $82,000 when oil retreated.

paxg.standing: The dollar price of a troy ounce of gold on New York's COMEX futures market. Gold pays no interest, so it tends to fall when yields and the dollar rise, and central banks and households buy it when they distrust currencies.
paxg.recent: Rate expectations did the pushing: energy-led inflation left markets pricing 80% odds of a December Fed hike, and higher rates make a metal that pays nothing costlier to hold, even with war in the headlines. China's central bank kept buying, adding 23 tonnes in September, and India ended tax relief on gold imports.

wiki-artificial-intelligence.standing: How many people open Wikipedia's article on artificial intelligence each day. It is the page readers land on when the technology itself, rather than one company or product, becomes the question.
wiki-artificial-intelligence.recent: China drafted curbs on exporting 23 AI technologies, model weights among them, and an Indian advisory said AI agents had read firms' live records undetected. SpaceX spent $16.4 billion on AI infrastructure in one quarter, while Microsoft dropped Nscale's site at Loughton because its grid connection was a decade away.

wiki-russia.standing: How many people open the Wikipedia article on Russia each day. It jumps when the country does something the wider world wants explained, so it marks which events reached people who do not follow the news closely.
wiki-russia.recent: Washington eased its pressure on Moscow: Trump paused Russian oil sanctions in a waiver Rubio called a 60-day pause, and the first 40,000 tonnes of Russian diesel head for the US. Putin freed Stephen Hubbard during Witkoff's visit, while Russian strikes on 28 energy facilities left 550,000 households in Ukraine without power.

wiki-strait-of-hormuz.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the channel between Iran and Oman through which Gulf oil and gas reach the open sea. About a fifth of the world's oil passes through it, and no sea route goes around it.
wiki-strait-of-hormuz.recent: Mines and Iranian fire hit shipping in the strait. The IRGC said a 2-million-barrel supertanker struck a mine, 12 ships were attacked in one week, and Iran's strait authority blacklisted 122 vessels. Tehran then offered to reopen Hormuz within 6 days on its own terms, while Gulf states sent Lavrov to press it and Brent sat above $109.

cp:hormuz.standing: One-fifth of global seaborne oil passes through this 21-mile strait between Iran and Oman.
cp:hormuz.recent: Iran's strait authority has blacklisted 122 ships, and the Guards say mines set 2 tankers ablaze, one a supertanker that burned. Qatar is sending gas to Poland through the Red Sea, Vitol puts shipping US crude to Asia at $40 a barrel, and Iran has offered to reopen Hormuz within 6 days on its own terms.

cp:bab-el-mandeb.standing: Between Yemen and Djibouti — the Red Sea’s southern gate. Houthi attacks since 2023 have pushed container shipping to reroute around Africa.
cp:bab-el-mandeb.recent: The war reached the strait's own shore. Yemen's government says its forces took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road, and the fighting killed 63 people in 24 hours. With Hormuz closed, Qatar has begun sending gas the other way round, through the Red Sea, and one tanker is now heading for Poland.

cp:suez.standing: Egypt’s 120-mile artery carries roughly 12% of global trade. The 2021 closure disrupted supply chains for weeks; Red Sea instability keeps it volatile.
cp:suez.recent: A Qatari gas tanker is crossing the Red Sea toward Poland, a route to Europe that runs through the canal. Its southern approach is now a war zone: missiles targeted Yanbu on Saudi Arabia's Red Sea coast, and Egypt's council approved troops for Saudi Arabia after Houthi attacks, though parliament has yet to vote.

cp:malacca.standing: Between Malaysia and Sumatra — the fastest route between the Indian and Pacific Oceans. Over 80,000 ships a year, including most of China’s oil imports.
cp:malacca.recent: The fortnight's tanker news came from the far end of Asia's oil route: mines set supertankers ablaze in Hormuz, and Vitol put the cost of shipping US crude to Asia at $40 a barrel as refiners turned to smaller tankers. None of it has thinned traffic through Malacca, and Singapore's worst haze since 2015 left no mark on it either.

cp:taiwan.standing: Between mainland China and Taiwan — roughly 40% of the world’s container traffic passes through, and the flashpoint of any US–China confrontation.
cp:taiwan.recent: The fortnight's China news included Beijing's sanctions on Paraguay's communications minister and Belize's foreign minister over their Taiwan ties, and a second submarine-drone mothership built at Guangzhou, but nothing about closures, exercises or rerouting in the strait itself, so none of it accounts for the traffic.

cp:panama.standing: 50-mile shortcut between the Atlantic and Pacific. Drought in 2023–24 cut daily transits by half — a live example of climate binding to trade.
cp:panama.recent: The 7.7 earthquake that toppled a tower in Penonomé and set off tsunami warnings across Latin America is the one Panama story of the period, and nothing in it reports damage to the canal or a halt to transits. Nothing else in the input accounts for the traffic.

cp:bosporus.standing: Istanbul’s 20-mile waterway links the Black Sea to the Mediterranean — the only route for Russian naval access and Ukrainian grain exports.
cp:bosporus.recent: Drones sank a ship off Bulgaria with 11 sailors missing, a tanker fire off Romania left 8 of the Wine Trader's 12 crew missing, and drones hit two more ships near Romania, which put the war on the grain corridor that feeds this strait. Germany urged Russia to halt the attacks, and NATO is sending planes and drones to the Black Sea.

cp:gibraltar.standing: 8 miles between Morocco and Spain — the only Atlantic–Mediterranean link. A surveillance chokepoint for Russian submarines and sanctioned oil.
cp:gibraltar.recent: Washington lifted sanctions on Russian diesel for a time, weighed easing them on the shadow-fleet tankers this strait is watched for, and Trump waived 500% tariffs on Russian energy. None of it accounts for the vessel count.

cp:dover.standing: The busiest shipping lane on Earth — 400+ ships a day squeeze through the English Channel’s 21-mile narrows.

cp:cape-of-good-hope.standing: The 3,000-mile detour around southern Africa — the alternative when the Red Sea is closed. The new default for tankers since Houthi attacks began.
cp:cape-of-good-hope.recent: This fortnight's tanker story was in the Strait of Hormuz, where the Revolutionary Guards say mines set supertankers ablaze. In Singapore, Vitol put the cost of shipping US crude to Asia at $40 a barrel. Neither explains the traffic around the Cape of Good Hope.

cp:kerch.standing: Between Crimea and Russia — the only access to the Sea of Azov. A flashpoint since 2014 and contested throughout the Russia–Ukraine war.
cp:kerch.recent: This fortnight's Black Sea news came from its western end. Drones sank a cargo ship off Krapets in Bulgaria, leaving 11 sailors missing, and NATO sent patrol planes and drones after the attacks on shipping. None of it concerns the strait or explains its traffic.

mkt:bist.standing: The 100 largest and most traded companies on Borsa İstanbul, Türkiye's only stock exchange. It is priced in lira, so the level carries the country's inflation as much as its earnings: read the direction, not the number.
mkt:bist.recent: Police raided the opposition broadcaster Halk TV and the state took it over, Ankara asked parliament to approve a defence pact with Pakistan and Saudi Arabia, and Turkey launched its first floating gas platform to double Sakarya output. None of those reports ties any of it to share prices.

mkt:bursa-malaysia.standing: The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index: the 30 largest companies on Bursa Malaysia, the national exchange in Kuala Lumpur. It is the world's largest market for Islamic finance instruments and the centre of the global sukuk trade.
mkt:bursa-malaysia.recent: The fortnight's news from Malaysia was a youth lawsuit over deforestation, the cost Bangladeshis pay for Malaysia jobs, and a Deepavali vs Diwali political row. None of it accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:idx.standing: Every company listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange in Jakarta, counted in one index. It is the market of the world's largest Muslim-majority country, and commodity producers and banks carry most of its weight.
mkt:idx.recent: After months of warnings, MSCI moved to cut Indonesia's status and remove it from its global indexes, the benchmarks foreign funds track when they decide what to hold. Stocks fell 10% to a six-year low on the news, and the next session brought an 11.6% drop, the worst day since 1998.

mkt:tse.standing: The Nikkei 225 tracks 225 large companies on the Tokyo Stock Exchange, Japan's main market, weighted by share price. Tokyo is Asia's largest exchange and the first major market to price each trading day.
mkt:tse.recent: Yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago, the Bank of Japan's rate is a 31-year high, and Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama says inflation is turning wage-driven, which points to higher rates still. In Seoul, Samsung and SK Hynix led a chip sell-off over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals.

mkt:hkex.standing: The Hang Seng Index tracks the largest and most traded companies on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. It is where mainland Chinese companies meet foreign capital, and the clearest daily read on sentiment toward China.
mkt:hkex.recent: Two things touched this market in the fortnight. Hong Kong's regulator froze HK$4.38 billion over suspected faked public-offering demand, and the EU planned measures to cut imports of Chinese hybrid cars by half. Neither accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:sse.standing: The SSE Composite tracks every share listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange, mainland China's main board. Largely closed to foreign investors, it follows domestic policy more than global risk appetite.
mkt:sse.recent: The slide ran against the data: September exports rose 36% and retail sales beat their forecast. The same days brought signs of strain, as the PBOC said it would lend to funds, not just banks, to backstop the bond market, and robot shares valued at 22 billion yuan found no bids at 12 billion.

mkt:krx.standing: The Korea Composite Stock Price Index: every company on the main board of the Korea Exchange in Seoul, weighted by size. Samsung and SK Hynix dominate it, so it moves with the global semiconductor cycle.
mkt:krx.recent: Two chip routs did most of the damage: Samsung and SK Hynix dragged the index down 5.5% on worries over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals, and two days later it plunged more than 7%. Both came within a week of Samsung forecasting a 780% quarterly operating profit jump on the AI boom, and Elice's listing then closed 30% below its offer.

mkt:bse.standing: The Sensitive Index: 30 of the largest companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, India. The exchange is Asia's oldest, founded in 1875, and this index is the benchmark for Indian equities.
mkt:bse.recent: India was set for back-to-back rate hikes as inflation risks mounted: food inflation reached 7.74% in September, up from 5.97%, with the Hormuz-driven fuel shock feeding prices. Big money still came in. Gulf sovereign funds bid for Jio Platforms' record offering, and Fairfax won 60.72% of IDBI Bank for ₹52,878 crore.

mkt:sgx.standing: The 30 largest and most traded companies on the Singapore Exchange, the main market of Southeast Asia's financial hub. Three banks and regional property groups carry most of its weight, so it moves with interest rates.
mkt:sgx.recent: Singapore's banks, which the index is weighted to, saw a hot rally stutter as bond yields surged. Haze from Indonesian fires and record tanker freight costs for Asian refiners dominated the city's other headlines, but neither accounts for the index.

mkt:twse.standing: The Taiwan Stock Exchange's capitalisation-weighted index of every common share listed in Taipei. TSMC alone is roughly a third of it, which makes this the most concentrated major market on the map.
mkt:twse.recent: Chip shares sold off across the region: Samsung and SK Hynix dragged South Korea's benchmark down 5.5%, and TSMC fell even after posting record profit for the sixth straight quarter. In Taoyuan, one of Micron's two Taiwan unions moved to strike as a bonus dispute escalated.

mkt:asx.standing: The 200 largest companies listed on the Australian Securities Exchange in Sydney, weighted by market value. Mining and banking dominate it, and it is often the first major market to react to Chinese demand data.
mkt:asx.recent: The fortnight's one piece of Sydney market news was Firmus scrapping its Australian listing after seeking a valuation 600 times its revenue. Nothing reported in the period accounts for the index's path.

mkt:jse.standing: The All Share index covers nearly every company listed on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange, South Africa's main market, weighted by size. It is Africa's largest exchange by far, and the only one with a usable public daily series.
mkt:jse.recent: The fortnight's South African news was political rather than corporate. The government withdrew an asylum directive after riots in Durban and Soweto, and cut the fuel levy until January 2027. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:b3.standing: The most traded shares on B3, the São Paulo exchange that is Latin America's largest, weighted by market value. Iron ore, oil and Brazilian interest rates drive it, through the miners, oil producers and banks that dominate it.
mkt:b3.recent: Brazil's presidential runoff dominated the fortnight: polls moved Flávio Bolsonaro narrowly ahead of Lula, his potential finance chief promised a fast fiscal policy fix, and business elites who had scorned him rushed to meet him. The Senate also voted 75 to 1 to end the six-day work week.

mkt:bmv.standing: The Índice de Precios y Cotizaciones tracks about 35 of the largest, most traded companies on the Bolsa Mexicana de Valores in Mexico City. It is Mexico's benchmark, tightly coupled to US demand and the peso.
mkt:bmv.recent: The fortnight's Mexican business news was AT&T selling its 24.7 million Mexican subscribers for $2 billion, and a decree giving Meta, TikTok and X a month to protect minors on their platforms. Neither accounts for the index's climb.

mkt:byma.standing: The S&P Merval tracks the most traded shares on Bolsas y Mercados Argentinos, Argentina's main exchange. Priced in a peso that has repeatedly lost most of its value, it rises even in bad years; only direction means much.
mkt:byma.recent: Argentina posted a second straight month of inflation below 2%, and it lodged a legal claim against the UK's Falklands oil exploration. Neither accounts for the index's slide.

mkt:tsx.standing: The broad benchmark of the Toronto Stock Exchange, Canada's main market, tracking around 200 of its largest companies by market value. Banks, oil producers and miners dominate it, so it trades like a commodity index.
mkt:tsx.recent: Albertans voted 76% to stay in Canada, defeating a separation push in the province that produces most of the index's energy weight. Gasoline also rose 27.8% in a year on war-driven fuel prices, which pushed Canadian inflation to 3.1%. Neither event is reported as the cause of the index's rise.

mkt:nyse.standing: The S&P 500 tracks 500 of the largest companies listed on the New York Stock Exchange and Nasdaq, weighted by market value. It is the largest equity market on earth, and its close sets the tone every other market opens against.
mkt:nyse.recent: Earnings season hit two of the index's heaviest names: Tesla's net profit fell 43%, and Meta's free cash flow turned negative a day after a New Mexico ruling cost it $25 billion. Warsh withheld Fed guidance, calling AI a shock to the economy, and Goldman expects $1.7 trillion in 2027 unlocks to be matched by buybacks.

mkt:lse.standing: The 100 largest companies listed on the London Stock Exchange, Britain's main market, ranked by market value. Most of their revenue is earned abroad, so a falling pound tends to push the index up.
mkt:lse.recent: The UK news of the fortnight was a Google Cloud failure that hit Revolut and banks, gas driving most of a rise in household bills, and Microsoft dropping an Nscale data-centre site over grid delays. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:xetra.standing: The Deutscher Aktienindex: the 40 largest companies on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange, Germany's main market. It is built on the country's industrial and chemical base, making it Europe's clearest export barometer.
mkt:xetra.recent: The fortnight's German business news was mixed: Volkswagen planned a pay freeze for 660,000 workers until 2030, Amazon pledged €16 billion for data centers and Prime, and the ECB defended its September hike with euro-zone inflation at 3.8%. None of it accounts for the index's path over the window.

mkt:euronext-paris.standing: The 40 largest companies listed on Euronext Paris, France's main stock market, weighted by the value of their freely traded shares. Luxury and energy groups dominate it, leaving it unusually exposed to Chinese consumer demand.
mkt:euronext-paris.recent: France's 10-year bond yield reached 4.96%, its highest since 2002, as protests over school funding and rents spread nationwide and ended in curfews and nearly 2,400 arrests. The European Central Bank heads for a December hike, which raises the cost of money for every company in the index.

mkt:euronext-amsterdam.standing: The Amsterdam Exchange index tracks the largest, most traded companies on Euronext Amsterdam, the Dutch market. It is the world's oldest exchange, now carried largely by chip-equipment maker ASML.
mkt:euronext-amsterdam.recent: Mid-October belonged to ASML, the index's heaviest name: China's share of its sales jumped from 14% to 23%, with its chip equipment sales there up 109% despite a US push for export curbs. Against that, Argenx saw its blockbuster Vyvgart fail to beat placebo in Sjögren's.

mkt:bme.standing: The 35 most liquid companies on the Bolsa de Madrid, Spain's main stock exchange. Its big banks earn much of their profit in Latin America, so the index moves with both regions.
mkt:bme.recent: Spain's news in the window was of floods in the east, where Pego took 632 mm of rain in 36 hours, and of the opposition leader backing De Cos to succeed Lagarde at the ECB; none of it accounts for the index.

mkt:borsa-italiana.standing: The 40 largest, most traded companies on Borsa Italiana in Milan, Italy's main market. Banks and utilities dominate it, making it the market most sensitive to Italian sovereign debt spreads.
mkt:borsa-italiana.recent: The fortnight in Italy brought cost-of-living protests that police met with tear gas in Milan, ending in 28 arrests, and an air traffic control failure that halved flights across the country. Nothing reported ties either event to the index's slide.

mkt:six.standing: The Swiss Market Index: the 20 largest companies on the SIX Swiss Exchange in Zurich, Switzerland's main market. Nestlé, Roche and Novartis carry it, which makes it defensive when the world turns risk-off.
mkt:six.recent: The one Swiss business story of the fortnight was the Swiss trade chief saying that Rolex and gold were meant for the US and not for Trump. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:nasdaq-stockholm.standing: The OMX Stockholm 30: the 30 most traded shares on Nasdaq Stockholm, Sweden's main stock exchange. Nordic industrials and telecoms weigh heavily in it, which makes it a useful early read on European capital spending.

mkt:tase.standing: The 125 largest companies by market value on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange, Israel's only stock market. It trades Sunday to Thursday and is heavily weighted to banks, defence and technology.
mkt:tase.recent: The fortnight's news from Israel ran up to the 27 October election: Trump endorsed Netanyahu and tied the vote to the war on Iran, Netanyahu published a doctrine making preemptive war official policy, and Hegseth visited days before polling. None of it is reported as moving the index.

wiki-donald-trump.standing: The number of people who open the Wikipedia article on Donald Trump, the US president, each day. It rises when he does something readers want to look up, a rough gauge of how far American politics is reaching a general audience.
wiki-donald-trump.recent: Trump waived 500% tariffs on Russian energy before they began, then sent Witkoff to Moscow after Ukraine talks in Oslo, where Kyiv suspected Washington had withheld warning of 16 ballistic missiles. He also promised jail for California officials who count flagged ballots and endorsed Netanyahu ahead of Israel's 27 October vote.

fed-funds.standing: The range the Federal Reserve sets for overnight lending between US banks. Every dollar borrowing cost is priced off it, from mortgages and Treasury yields to the debts of governments and companies far outside the United States.
fed-funds.recent: Gasoline pushed US prices up 3.7% over the year to September, and markets now put 80% odds on a December hike. Warsh, speaking at the IMF meetings in Bangkok, called AI a shock to the economy and vowed price stability without guiding on rates, while Trump convened a panel to hear the case for removing Governor Lisa Cook.

ecb-rate.standing: The interest the European Central Bank pays commercial banks on money parked with it overnight, and the rate that steers borrowing costs across the euro zone. Mortgages, business loans and government bond yields move after it.
ecb-rate.recent: The European Central Bank raised rates in September with euro-zone inflation at 3.8%, nearly double its target, and its officials called the hike proportionate. Lagarde has since pointed to a bond selloff as the bank heads for a December hike, while governments have until 28 October to nominate Isabel Schnabel's replacement.

us-unemployment.standing: The share of the American labour force without a job and actively looking for one, from a monthly household survey. It is one half of the Federal Reserve's mandate, so interest rates move with it.

xag.standing: The price of a troy ounce of silver on New York's COMEX futures market. It is part precious metal and part industrial input, used in solar panels and electronics, so it moves with gold and with factory demand.

us-cpi.standing: The yearly rise in the Consumer Price Index, the Bureau of Labor Statistics' monthly measure of what American households pay. The Federal Reserve sets interest rates against it, and borrowing costs worldwide follow.
us-cpi.recent: Gasoline drove September's reading: prices rose 0.6% in that month alone, more than expected. The figure landed weeks before the midterm elections and revived bets on a Fed rate hike, and stocks in Mainland China and Hong Kong fell the next day on fears of tighter policy.

portwatch-hormuz-tanker.standing: A daily count of oil tankers passing the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow channel between Iran and Oman. About a fifth of the world's oil leaves the Gulf through it, so a drop here reaches fuel prices in Asia first.
portwatch-hormuz-tanker.recent: The strait is under a prolonged closure: Iran's strait authority has blacklisted 122 vessels, and the Revolutionary Guards say their mines set a supertanker ablaze. A record 12 ships were attacked near Hormuz in one week, and shipping US crude to Asia now costs $40 a barrel, Vitol says, while Iran offers terms to reopen within 6 days.

portwatch-bab-container.standing: Container ships crossing the strait between Yemen and Djibouti each day, the southern gate of the Red Sea and the Suez route between Asia and Europe. When it is unsafe, lines divert around Africa and freight takes weeks longer.
portwatch-bab-container.recent: The Houthis' strikes this fortnight landed on Saudi Arabia: Riyadh airport, the East-West pipeline to Yanbu and the Shaybah oilfield. With Hormuz closed, the Red Sea has become a bypass, and a Qatari gas tanker is crossing it toward Poland. None of these stories reports an attack on container ships in the strait itself.

portwatch-suez-total.standing: The number of ships passing each day through Egypt's canal between the Mediterranean and the Red Sea, the short route between Asia and Europe. When it falls, cargo is going round Africa, adding days and fuel to every voyage.
portwatch-suez-total.recent: The news from the region was the Houthi war on Saudi Arabia: strikes on Riyadh airport, the Shaybah oilfield and the East-West pipeline to Yanbu. None of it reported an attack on shipping or a change at the canal that would account for the traffic.

portwatch-panama-total.standing: Ships crossing the Panama Canal each day, the shortcut between the Atlantic and the Pacific. Its locks run on fresh water from Gatún Lake, so drought in Panama cuts the daily slots and delays trade between Asia and the US east coast.
portwatch-panama-total.recent: A 7.7 earthquake struck Panama, toppled a tower in Penonomé and set off tsunami warnings across Latin America. The UN also called for action against an 'off the charts' El Niño, the kind of weather that leaves the locks short of rain. Nothing reported links either event to the number of ships crossing.

portwatch-malacca-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the strait between Malaysia and Indonesia's Sumatra, the shortest sea route from the Indian Ocean to the Pacific. Most oil East Asia imports from the Middle East goes through it.
portwatch-malacca-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news was about Hormuz, where Iran's Guards said mines set tankers ablaze and Vitol put the cost of shipping US crude to Asia at $40 a barrel, squeezing Asian refiners. None of it explains the traffic through Malacca.

portwatch-taiwan-total.standing: The count of cargo ships and tankers passing each day between Taiwan and mainland China. The strait is the main lane between the ports of north-east Asia and the routes south, and typhoons and military drills both empty it.

portwatch-dover-total.standing: The narrowest part of the English Channel, between England and France, and one of the busiest shipping lanes in the world. Most cargo sailing between the Atlantic and the ports of northern Europe passes through it.

portwatch-gibraltar-total.standing: The count of ships passing each day through the 14-kilometre gap between Spain and Morocco, the only sea route between the Atlantic and the Mediterranean. Traffic bound to or from the Suez Canal passes here too.
portwatch-gibraltar-total.recent: The fortnight's shipping news came from Hormuz, where Iran blacklisted 122 ships and mines set tankers ablaze. None of it reaches the traffic through Gibraltar or explains the September dip.

wiki-houthi-movement.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on the Houthis, the Zaydi Shia armed movement that holds Sanaa and northern Yemen. Its missiles reach the Bab el-Mandeb strait, the southern gate to the Red Sea and Suez.
wiki-houthi-movement.recent: A Houthi strike on Riyadh's airport killed 13 people and grounded 82% of Monday's flights, with Qatar Airways suspending service to Riyadh and Dammam. The war then reached Dhahran, where a missile set fire to an Aramco building; Saudi Arabia postponed its investor summit to 2027, and the US ordered non-emergency staff and families out.

wiki-inflation.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on inflation, the general rise in prices that erodes what money buys. Traffic climbs when price rises and central-bank rate decisions reach households, so it tracks public worry about living costs.
wiki-inflation.recent: The spike followed US figures showing prices up 3.7% over the year to September, driven by gasoline, which revived bets on a Fed hike before the midterm elections. Fuel pushed inflation up elsewhere too, to 3.1% in Canada and 11.38% in Pakistan, as Hormuz stayed closed and the IMF warned of war spillovers.

wiki-ukraine.standing: How many times a day Wikipedia's article on Ukraine is opened. Readers arrive when the country's war with Russia, its grain exports or its diplomacy turn up in the news, so the count marks when the world looks its way.
wiki-ukraine.recent: Russia struck 28 energy facilities and cut power to 550,000 households, while Ukrainian drones set a St Petersburg oil terminal alight. Talks moved to Oslo, Witkoff met Putin in Moscow, and Trump put on hold the new Russia sanctions he had signed into law. In Kyiv, detectives searched the National Bank.

xmr.standing: A cryptocurrency built to hide the sender, receiver and amount of every transaction. That privacy makes it the coin of choice for ransomware crews and darknet markets, and the one exchanges delist under regulatory pressure.

poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the truce between the United States and Iran survives to a set date. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves with every strike, ship seizure and round of talks in the Gulf.
poly-us-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-throu.recent: Iran offered to reopen Hormuz within 6 days as Gulf states pressed Lavrov to lean on Tehran. A day later the Guards said mines set 2 tankers ablaze and 122 ships were blacklisted, and Tehran told Asim Munir, carrying mediators' proposals, that no enriched uranium will leave, the sticking point in any deal.

poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether the United States lifts its blockade of Iran before a set deadline. The price is what traders will pay for a yes, and it moves with every sign of a deal or of escalation in the Gulf.
poly-us-announces-end-of-iranian-blockad.recent: Talks to end the war stalled on uranium: Iran told Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir, carrying mediators' proposals, that no enriched uranium will leave. Its offer to reopen Hormuz within 6 days came as its strait authority blacklisted 122 ships and the Guards said mines set 2 tankers ablaze.

poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the ceasefire between Israel and Iran is still in force on October 31. Its price is what traders will stake on the truce surviving, and it moves on strikes, talks and threats from either side.
poly-israel-x-iran-ceasefire-continues-t.recent: Pete Hegseth visited Netanyahu unannounced as the Guards claimed mines set 2 tankers ablaze in Hormuz. A day later Tehran told Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir that no enriched uranium will leave Iran, the sticking point in any deal, and Mohsen Rezaei said Iran expects a US-Israeli strike before the US midterms.

co:nvidia.standing: Designs the processors that most artificial-intelligence models are trained and run on, and sells them to the companies building data centres. It designs chips and does not make them: TSMC does.
co:nvidia.recent: Two threats to its sales landed in the same week. In China, Huawei shipped 572,000 AI accelerators in six months and took share from Nvidia there, and Microsoft said it will deploy its own Maia chips in Azure by the gigawatt, work Nvidia's processors would otherwise do.

co:apple.standing: Makes the iPhone, which brings in about half its sales, along with Mac computers, iPads and watches, and takes a cut of what is sold through its App Store.
co:apple.recent: Pre-orders for the iPhone Duo opened and the phone was soon backordered until 2027. The same week Apple introduced HomeView, a $299 tablet for the home, and began a China beta of Apple Intelligence that runs on Alibaba's Qwen models, the route by which its AI features reach Chinese buyers.

co:alphabet.standing: Owns Google and YouTube. Most of its money comes from advertising beside search results and videos; it also sells cloud computing and builds its own AI models.
co:alphabet.recent: Google's only UK cloud region failed on Tuesday, taking several Cloud services in Europe down with it. A week earlier Google halved Gemini 4 Argon's price to $2 per million input tokens, while its own benchmarks put Claude 9 points ahead of it. Neither event accounts for the share's path.

co:amazon.standing: An online retailer, and through Amazon Web Services the largest seller of cloud computing, which earns most of its profit.
co:amazon.recent: Amazon built its 1,000th satellite and is weeks from a space Internet rollout under Amazon Leo. It shuffled its Alexa leadership after a tablet release, and was reported to be weighing $7 billion for the AI startup Decart. None of that news explains the share price.

co:tsmc.standing: Manufactures the chips other companies design, among them Apple’s, Nvidia’s and AMD’s, and makes most of the world’s most advanced ones, in Taiwan.
co:tsmc.recent: TSMC reported a record profit for the sixth straight quarter in mid-October, and the shares fell after the result rather than rising on it. Nothing in the reports that carried the figures says what sellers objected to.

co:microsoft.standing: Sells Windows and Office, and rents out computing power through Azure, one of the largest clouds. It holds a large stake in OpenAI.
co:microsoft.recent: Washington suspended Microsoft from its green card scheme amid fraud claims, and the shares fell 7.5% after the suspension. Days later Microsoft said it would deploy its own Maia AI chips by the gigawatt. It then dropped Nscale's planned AI site in Loughton, Essex, where a grid connection won't come until the 2030s.

co:broadcom.standing: Makes the networking chips that connect data centres and designs custom AI chips for companies such as Google. It also owns the software firm VMware.

co:spacex.standing: Builds reusable rockets, launches satellites and astronauts for governments and companies, and runs Starlink, a satellite internet network.
co:spacex.recent: A nationwide low-band spectrum deal for Starlink Mobile lifted the shares while Verizon and AT&T fell. SpaceX then reported revenue doubling as it spent $16.4 billion on AI infrastructure in a quarter, while Ukraine accused it of throttling Starlink terminals and India still withheld the clearance it needs to sell service.

co:meta.standing: Owns Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, used by more than three billion people, and earns nearly all its money from advertising on them.
co:meta.recent: A New Mexico court ordered Meta to pay $25 billion over Cambridge Analytica, counting 43 million deception violations. The bill lands as its free cash flow fell to negative $2.12 billion, after a 14-month push to take its Muse AI model to the frontier.

co:aramco.standing: Saudi Arabia’s state oil company, which pumps more oil than any other company. The government owns nearly all of it, and its dividends pay for much of the kingdom’s budget.
co:aramco.recent: A missile set fire to an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran after the Saudi-led coalition hit a Houthi site. Four days later the Houthis told Aramco shareholders to sell, a warning carried by Iran's state agency Mehr. A Houthi drone strike near the Shaybah field followed.

co:tesla.standing: Makes electric cars, and the batteries that store power for homes and electricity grids. Led by Elon Musk, who also leads SpaceX.
co:tesla.recent: Tesla's third-quarter net profit fell 43% to $787 million: it sold fewer cars than a year earlier, cut prices and spent on AI, and its energy-storage business shrank. On the same day, reports said SpaceX and Tesla were exploring a merger. The week before, it unveiled the 2026 Roadster, a sports car priced from $200,000.

co:samsung.standing: One of the three companies that make most of the world’s memory chips, and one of the largest makers of smartphones and televisions.
co:samsung.recent: Samsung forecast a quarterly operating profit of 107.4 trillion won, a 780% jump driven by AI demand for its memory chips. Five days later it and SK Hynix led a selloff that took South Korea's benchmark index down 5.5%, as worries over AI spending and Chinese memory rivals hit the chipmakers.

co:micron.standing: The one large American maker of memory chips, the kind that hold data in phones, computers and AI data centres. Its two main rivals are Samsung and SK Hynix.
co:micron.recent: One of Micron's two unions in Taiwan called a strike for Thursday as a dispute over bonuses escalated, putting work at its Taoyuan operations in question. Nothing reported over the period explains the share's earlier slide.

co:amd.standing: Designs processors for computers and data centres, where it competes with Intel, and AI chips, where it competes with Nvidia. Like Nvidia, it has TSMC make them.

co:berkshire.standing: A holding company built by Warren Buffett. It owns insurers, a railway and energy utilities outright, and holds large stakes in companies such as Apple and Coca-Cola.

co:lilly.standing: An American drugmaker. Its diabetes and weight-loss medicines, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, account for much of its growth.
co:lilly.recent: Lilly is testing a cousin of its obesity drug against alcohol use disorder. That widens what the GLP-1 class is meant to treat, but none of the fortnight's news accounts for the share price.

co:jpmorgan.standing: The largest bank in the United States by assets, serving households, companies and governments.

co:skhynix.standing: A South Korean maker of memory chips, and the main supplier of the high-speed memory that Nvidia’s AI chips need.
co:skhynix.recent: On 13 October Samsung and SK Hynix pulled South Korea's benchmark stock index down 5.5% in one session, as doubts about AI spending met the threat of cheaper Chinese memory rivals, the two forces that set the price of the chips SK Hynix sells.

co:walmart.standing: The world’s largest retailer by sales, with thousands of stores in the United States and abroad.
co:walmart.recent: Walmart said it would cover 250-plus medications, including GLP-1s and insulin, at no cost for its workers, an addition to employee benefits rather than a change to its sales. Nothing reported in the period explains the share price.

co:asml.standing: A Dutch company, and the only maker of the machines needed to print the most advanced chips. Every leading chipmaker buys from it, and its sales to China are restricted.
co:asml.recent: Its chip equipment sales to China rose 109%, lifting China's share of its sales from 14% to 23%, even as the US pushed for wider export curbs. The same week, demand for AI chips had made it a European AI industry darling, with its order book tied to the build-out.

us-2y.standing: The interest rate the US government pays to borrow for two years. Of all Treasury yields it follows the Federal Reserve's policy rate most closely, so it shows where traders are betting that rate goes next.

us-mortgage.standing: The average interest rate US lenders charge on a 30-year fixed home loan, the mortgage most American buyers take. It follows long-dated Treasury yields, and it sets what a house costs each month and whether owners can afford to move.

ez-cpi.standing: The annual rise in consumer prices across the countries that share the euro, measured by Eurostat on one harmonised basket. The European Central Bank aims for 2% and sets the bloc's interest rates against it.

bnb.standing: The native token of BNB Chain, the blockchain network built by the exchange Binance. Holders use it to pay transaction fees on the chain and get trading discounts on Binance, so its price follows the exchange's fortunes and its regulators.

trx.standing: The token of the Tron blockchain, a network built for cheap, fast transfers. Most of its traffic is the dollar stablecoin Tether, so its price follows demand for moving dollars outside banks, especially in emerging markets.

sol.standing: The token of the Solana blockchain, used to pay its transaction fees and staked by the validators that secure it. Its price is a bet on how much trading and payment traffic the network wins, and it swings harder than Bitcoin.
sol.recent: The fall came with a crypto-wide sell-off in which nearly $1 billion in crypto bets were liquidated as bitcoin, ether and XRP slid. The network's own news was technical and did not hold the price up: a change that halves block times, then the Alpenglow upgrade, set for Oct. 21 and targeting 150-millisecond finality.

xrp.standing: The native token of the XRP Ledger, a payments network built for fast cross-border transfers. Ripple, the company most closely tied to it, holds a large share of the supply, so its legal and commercial fortunes move the price.
xrp.recent: The mid-October slide was market-wide: nearly $1 billion in leveraged crypto bets were liquidated as bitcoin, ether and XRP fell together. The ledger also faced its own problem, a years-old bug that threatened the 100 billion XRP cap, and its fix was pushed to November after validator support dipped for two hours.

hype.standing: The token of Hyperliquid, a blockchain built to run a derivatives exchange where traders bet on crypto prices with leverage. Trading fees fund buybacks of the token, so its price follows how much business the exchange does.
hype.recent: The fortnight's one story about the venue was a Bloomberg Business profile of Jeff Yan's plan to bring the entire financial industry onto Hyperliquid, an ambition rather than an event. Nothing in it explains the token's slide.

doge.standing: A cryptocurrency launched as a joke around a Shiba Inu dog meme, with no cap on how many coins can exist. It has little use beyond payments and tipping, so its price moves on online attention and celebrity endorsement.

zec.standing: A cryptocurrency built on Bitcoin's design, with the same 21 million coin cap, that lets users hide sender, receiver and amount using zero-knowledge proofs. It is the main market price put on financial privacy on a public blockchain.
zec.recent: The slide into mid-October came during a market-wide washout: nearly $1 billion in leveraged crypto bets were liquidated as bitcoin, ether and XRP fell together. ZEC then jumped 11% in a single day as AI earnings revived tech stocks and bitcoin held around $83,000.

boe-rate.standing: Bank Rate, the interest the Bank of England pays commercial banks on their reserves, set by its nine-member Monetary Policy Committee. British mortgage, savings and business loan rates are priced off it, and sterling moves with it.
boe-rate.recent: The Bank of England has held since its last cut, but its officials divided this month over the inflation risk facing the UK, and Greene said those risks were bigger than thought. The pressure is energy: gas explains £161 of a £180 rise in UK bills, the kind of shock that has some asking why a central bank would hike into it.

link.standing: The token of Chainlink, a network of oracles that feeds outside data such as prices into blockchain smart contracts. Node operators are paid in it, and much of decentralised lending relies on its price feeds.

boj-rate.standing: The Bank of Japan's short-term policy rate, the price of overnight money in yen. Kept near zero for decades, it made the yen the world's cheapest currency to borrow, so a rise pulls money back to Japan from markets everywhere.
boj-rate.recent: Yen-priced imports cost 24.5% more than a year ago, keeping wholesale inflation elevated, and Ueda said the BOJ 'can't tolerate' underlying inflation running further over 2%. The IMF added that the bank may need to tighten faster, and the finance minister now says Japan is shifting to wage-driven inflation, the kind a central bank answers with rates.

tcmb-rate.standing: The one-week repo rate at which the Central Bank of the Republic of Türkiye lends to commercial banks, and the country's main policy rate. It sets the cost of lira credit and shapes how attractive the currency is to hold against inflation.

pboc-rate.standing: The one-year loan prime rate, the benchmark the People's Bank of China steers and that banks use to price most new business and household loans. It sets the cost of credit across the world's second-largest economy.
pboc-rate.recent: The People's Bank of China's October moves left the rate alone. It said it will lend to funds, not just banks, to steady the bond market, and it bought 23 tonnes of gold in September. Neither step changes the price of a loan.

bcb-rate.standing: The Selic, the overnight rate the Central Bank of Brazil sets to steer inflation toward its target. It prices government debt and bank lending across Latin America's largest economy, and the real's appeal to foreign money rises and falls with it.

bi-rate.standing: The rate Bank Indonesia sets for seven-day lending to commercial banks, its main policy tool. It steers borrowing costs across Southeast Asia's largest economy and is used to defend the rupiah when capital flows out.

cbr-rate.standing: The Bank of Russia's key rate, the price at which it lends to and takes deposits from commercial banks for a week. Rouble mortgages, company loans and the government's own borrowing costs are all priced off it.
cbr-rate.recent: The Bank of Russia's recent headlines were about its yuan purchases and its reports of growing freight turnover and a four-year high in petroleum product shipments from Far Eastern ports. None of them concern the rate decision itself.

mkt:set.standing: A capitalisation-weighted index of every common stock on the Stock Exchange of Thailand in Bangkok, the country's main market. It is sensitive to tourism flows and regional energy prices.
mkt:set.recent: The IMF and World Bank held their meetings in Bangkok this month, dominated by the Hormuz closure, poor-country debt and AI, but none of it concerned Thailand's own companies or economy, and none of it accounts for the index.

mkt:tadawul.standing: The Tadawul All Share Index covers every company on the Saudi Exchange's main market in Riyadh, the Arab world's largest by value and dominated by Aramco. It trades Sunday to Thursday, opening the global week before Tokyo.
mkt:tadawul.recent: Houthi strikes reached Saudi soil. An attack on Riyadh's airport killed 13 people, a missile set fire to an Aramco building in Dhahran, and a drone hit Shaybah. The Houthis told Aramco shareholders to sell, the kingdom postponed its investor summit to 2027, and the US ordered non-emergency staff and families out.

mkt:dfm.standing: The main index of the Dubai Financial Market, the stock exchange in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. It is the Gulf's main listing venue for property and banking, and trades Monday to Friday, unlike Riyadh.
mkt:dfm.recent: The fortnight's news from the Emirates was the Iran war's cost to its economy: non-oil output shrank 1.1% in the second quarter, Hormuz traffic fell to seven ships in a day, and Dubai inflation held above 5% on fuel. None of it accounts for the index's path.

mkt:pse.standing: The PSEi tracks 30 large companies listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange in Manila, the country's only bourse. It is a small, domestically driven market, and remittance flows from Filipinos working abroad move the index.
mkt:pse.recent: Manila's autumn brought protest and hardship. 17,000 police met tens of thousands protesting US-backed data centres on 21 September, 22.6% of Filipino families went involuntarily hungry in September, and China called relations a 'critical juncture'. None of the reporting ties any of it to the index's fall.

stocks:META.standing: The owner of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp, which earns nearly all its revenue selling ads to reach more than three billion daily users. Its spending on AI data centres is among the heaviest in the industry.
stocks:META.recent: A New Mexico judge ordered Meta to pay $25 billion for deceiving Facebook users over the Cambridge Analytica breach, counting 43 million violations under state consumer-protection law. A day later the company reported free cash flow of negative $2.12 billion as it pours money into its Muse AI models.

stocks:MSFT.standing: The world's largest software company, maker of Windows, Office and the Azure cloud, and OpenAI's biggest backer. Its share is among the heaviest weights in US indices, so index funds worldwide move with it.
stocks:MSFT.recent: Microsoft said it would deploy its own Maia AI accelerator racks by the gigawatt across Azure. Earlier, the US barred it from the green card scheme amid fraud claims. Later, it dropped Nscale's Loughton site, where grid power for its AI campus may wait a decade.

poly-will-pedro-sanchez-be-the-next-prim.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Pedro Sánchez, Spain's Socialist prime minister, heads the government formed after the next general election. The price is what traders pay for a yes, and it moves on polls, coalition arithmetic and court cases.

poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if the Federal Reserve leaves its policy rate unchanged at one scheduled meeting. Its price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves on jobs data, inflation prints and officials' speeches.
poly-will-there-be-no-change-in-fed-inte.recent: In Bangkok, Warsh called AI a shock to the economy and withheld guidance on the Fed's next move, while the IMF praised his focus on price stability. Nearly all economists in a Reuters poll now say the Fed will skip October and raise rates again in December, with the AI boom adding to an inflation headache.

poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.standing: A contract that pays out if Russian and NATO forces clash directly before its deadline. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, and it moves with incidents on the alliance's border and with Ukraine talks.
poly-nato-x-russia-military-clash-by-oct.recent: The war drifted toward the table: Germany and Ukraine pressed Putin to join a full energy-sector truce, Trump put on hold new Russia sanctions he had signed into law, and Witkoff met Putin after talks in Oslo. The Kremlin, as reported, said it would return to US-mediated talks around 10 November, possibly in Abu Dhabi.

stocks:0700.HK.standing: The Shenzhen company behind WeChat, the app most of China uses to message and pay, and the world's largest video-game publisher by revenue. Its Hong Kong share is one of the heaviest weights in the Hang Seng index.
stocks:0700.HK.recent: Tencent spent the fortnight narrowing its AI agents. It set the QClaw desktop agent to shut on 24 December, added WorkBuddy to WeCom's contact list and offered developers 2,000 free search calls a month, while Meta's Muse pushed ByteDance and Tencent to respond. None of that accounts for the share price.

stocks:BABA.standing: China's largest e-commerce company, owner of the Taobao and Tmall marketplaces and of the country's biggest cloud business. Its New York-listed share is the one most foreign investors use to take a view on Chinese consumers and tech.
stocks:BABA.recent: Alibaba sued the Pentagon over being classified as a Chinese military affiliate, denying any link to the Chinese military. Apple's AI features in China launched on its Qwen models, and its N1 Pro glasses went on sale verifying payments by iris scan. None of it, as reported, accounts for the share's slide.

stocks:AMZN.standing: The world's largest online retailer and, through Amazon Web Services, the largest seller of rented computing power. The cloud arm earns most of the profit, so the share moves on data-centre demand more than on shopping.
stocks:AMZN.recent: Amazon pledged €16 billion in Germany for data centers and Prime, the week's largest commitment. Earlier in the month it shuffled Alexa leadership after a high-end tablet release, was reported weighing $7 billion for the AI startup Decart, and said Amazon Leo was weeks from launch, building 27 satellites a week.

poly-will-flavio-bolsonaro-win-the-secon.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Flávio Bolsonaro wins Brazil's presidential election by a margin of four to eight percentage points. It prices how close the race is, not just who wins.
poly-will-flavio-bolsonaro-win-the-secon.recent: The fortnight's reporting from Brazil's runoff centred on Meta: researchers logged over 1,000 Meta restrictions on political content, and Meta then admitted its AI had generated images favouring Flávio Bolsonaro. Neither story accounts for the swings in what traders will pay on his margin.

stocks:SPCX.standing: The rocket and satellite company founded by Elon Musk. It launches most of the world's orbital payloads on reusable Falcon rockets and runs Starlink, the satellite internet network that supplies most of its revenue.
stocks:SPCX.recent: A nationwide low-band spectrum deal for Starlink Mobile lifted the shares 4% in a day as Verizon and AT&T fell 7%. Quarterly revenue doubled, but SpaceX poured $16.4 billion into AI infrastructure, and Ukraine accused it of throttling Starlink for drones on military missions.

poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Democrats win both the Senate and the House in the 2026 US midterms. The price is what traders will pay for that outcome, which would give one party control of legislation and confirmations.
poly-2026-balance-of-power-d-senate-d-ho.recent: The fortnight's news about prediction markets concerned whether they are legal, not the races: 39 states and 145 tribal nations urged the Supreme Court to take up the question, and Kalshi's CEO said state-led oversight would push the markets out. None of it bears on the House or Senate contests this contract prices.

stocks:2222.SR.standing: Saudi Arabia's state oil company, the world's largest crude producer, listed on the Saudi Exchange in Riyadh since 2019. The state keeps almost all of it, so the small float trades on oil prices and the dividend.
stocks:2222.SR.recent: The war reached the company's own sites: a missile set fire to an Aramco administrative building in Dhahran, and a Houthi drone strike near the Shaybah field pushed Brent above $110. In between, the Houthis told Aramco shareholders to sell, Mehr reported, and the kingdom's output sank to a record 6.24 million barrels daily.

stocks:COIN.standing: The largest US cryptocurrency exchange, listed on Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from trading fees and the interest on USDC stablecoin reserves, so its shares rise and fall with crypto prices and trading volume.

stocks:NVDA.standing: The American designer of the graphics processors that train and run most of the world's AI models. Data-centre chips earn most of its revenue, so its share price is read as a gauge of what the industry spends on AI.
stocks:NVDA.recent: In China, Nvidia's share of AI chip sales fell as Huawei shipped 572,000 AI accelerators in six months, a homegrown rival taking ground in one of Nvidia's largest markets.

poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Benjamin Netanyahu heads the government formed after Israel's next election. The premiership needs a 61-seat Knesset majority, so coalition arithmetic moves it as much as votes do.
poly-will-benjamin-netanyahu-be-the-next.recent: Days before the election, Trump endorsed Netanyahu, and US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth met him secretly at a south Israel airbase without the army chief. The opposition called his new security doctrine 'empty slogans', and ex-Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar sued him for 3 million shekels. None of it accounts for where traders priced him.

stocks:RELIANCE.NS.standing: India's most valuable listed company, a Mumbai conglomerate that runs the Jamnagar refining complex alongside Jio telecoms and India's biggest retail chain. Its size makes it a swing stock for the whole Indian market.
stocks:RELIANCE.NS.recent: Jio Platforms priced India's largest share sale, seeking up to ₹30,213 crore, and drew nearly Rs 2.5 lakh crore of demand that included sovereign funds. Reliance said its satellite service awaits the same clearances as Starlink, and Rubio pressed India's refiners to process Venezuelan crude. None of it explains the share's dip.

stocks:TSLA.standing: Shares in Tesla, the US maker of electric cars and grid batteries, listed on Nasdaq. Its valuation rests more on bets about self-driving cars and robots than on the cars it sells today, so it moves on Elon Musk's promises.
stocks:TSLA.recent: Tesla unveiled the Roadster, a sports car priced at $200,000 or more. Then its quarterly net profit fell 43% to $787 million on fewer cars sold, price cuts and AI spending, and its energy-storage business shrank. The same day, reports said Tesla and SpaceX were exploring a merger that would combine about 30,000 bitcoin on their books.

stocks:AAPL.standing: Apple's shares, traded on the Nasdaq. Most of its revenue comes from the iPhone, and its weight as one of the world's most valuable companies means its moves carry the S&P 500 and Nasdaq indices with it.
stocks:AAPL.recent: The peak came the day iPhone Duo pre-orders opened and the phone sold out until 2027. The same day, Apple Intelligence launched in China, running on Alibaba's Qwen models. Three days earlier Apple introduced HomeView, a $299 tablet for the home.

stocks:3350.T.standing: A Tokyo-listed company that turned from running budget hotels to holding bitcoin as its main asset, and sells new shares to buy more. Its stock works as a leveraged bet on bitcoin for investors in Japan.
stocks:3350.T.recent: MSCI finalised rules that can eject companies whose main business is holding bitcoin from its equity indexes, Metaplanet among them. Index funds then sell the shares, not the bitcoin, which cuts at the cheap equity the firm raises to buy more; JPMorgan put the forced selling of Strategy alone at $2.8 billion.

stocks:HSBA.L.standing: One of Europe's largest banks, headquartered in London but earning most of its profit in Asia, above all in Hong Kong. Its London shares move on Asian interest rates and on the state of relations between China and the West.

stocks:JD.standing: One of China's largest online retailers, listed in New York and Hong Kong. Unlike its rivals it owns its warehouses and delivery fleet, so its sales track what Chinese households are spending.
stocks:JD.recent: The fortnight carried one story about the company's own business: it ended deposit pre-sales for its 18th Singles' Day. That story ran after the shares had already peaked, and nothing in it accounts for the price.

wiki-india.standing: Wikipedia's article on India, the world's most populous country and its largest democracy. How many people open it each day is a rough measure of how often the wider world stops to look the country up.
wiki-india.recent: Delhi spent the fortnight policing the 'cockroach' movement: CJP leaders were detained over protests against voter lists, 6,000 police blocked their flag march, and Abhijeet Dipke's detention became an arrest. Rubio then linked India's Russian oil waiver to its trade deal and pressed Reliance to refine Venezuelan crude.

stocks:V.standing: The largest card payment network in the world, routing transactions between the banks that issue cards and those that accept them. It earns a fee on each payment and lends nothing, so its revenue tracks consumer spending.

stocks:CRCL.standing: The US company that issues USDC, a dollar stablecoin backed by cash and short-dated Treasuries. Most of its revenue is interest on those reserves, so the share tracks US short-term rates and how much USDC circulates.

poly-will-rebeca-grynspan-be-the-next-se.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Rebeca Grynspan, the Costa Rican economist heading UN Trade and Development, becomes the next UN Secretary-General. The Security Council's five veto holders must all accept the nominee.

poly-ilhan-omar-federally-charged-by-oct.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if federal prosecutors charge Ilhan Omar, the Democratic congresswoman from Minnesota, before its deadline. The price is what traders pay for that payout.

poly-edi-rama-out-as-albania-pm-in-2026.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Edi Rama stops being Albania's prime minister before the end of 2026. Rama, leader of the Socialist Party, took office in 2013.

poly-yemeni-forces-enter-sanaa-by-novemb.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Yemen's government and allied forces enter Sanaa, the capital the Houthis have held since 2014, by November 30. Its price is what traders will pay on the city changing hands.
poly-yemeni-forces-enter-sanaa-by-novemb.recent: The government's claimed gains came on the coast, where it said it took Dhubab and cut the Mocha road toward Bab al-Mandeb, far from Sanaa. Meanwhile the Houthis carried the war into Saudi Arabia: a strike on Riyadh's airport stopped Lufthansa and Air India flights, and missiles and drones targeted the oil route at Yanbu.

stocks:LYFT.standing: Shares in Lyft, the second-largest ride-hailing app in the United States after Uber, sold almost entirely on the US and Canadian market. Its price turns on rider demand, driver pay and rules for gig workers.

stocks:UBER.standing: Shares in Uber, the largest ride-hailing and food-delivery platform outside China, listed in New York. The price tracks how many trips and orders it brokers and how much of each fare it keeps.
stocks:UBER.recent: The one story about Uber's own business came after the last close shown. Consumer Reports looked into how its AI pricing sets fares and found that same-minute quotes for one trip differed by 42.4%. Nothing earlier in the input accounts for the share price.

poly-iran-oman-hormuz-agreement-by-octob.standing: A Polymarket contract on whether Iran and Oman, the two states whose coasts form the Strait of Hormuz, reach an agreement on the strait before its deadline. About a fifth of the world's seaborne oil passes through that channel.
poly-iran-oman-hormuz-agreement-by-octob.recent: Iran and Oman agreed a 'safe route' through Hormuz, but the strait has turned more hostile since: mines set tankers ablaze, Iran's strait authority blacklisted 122 ships, and Tehran offered to reopen it within 6 days on its own terms. The mediation now runs through Russia's Lavrov and Pakistan's army chief Asim Munir rather than Oman.

wiki-volodymyr-zelenskyy.standing: Daily readers of the Wikipedia article on Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the former actor and comedian elected Ukraine's president in 2019, who has led the country through Russia's full-scale invasion.
wiki-volodymyr-zelenskyy.recent: Zelenskyy said Russia struck a Kharkiv power plant after Trump's energy truce, the same day South Korea recalled its Kyiv envoy for the first time since 2008. Ukraine later got no US warning of 16 incoming ballistic missiles, Bessent rebuked Zelenskyy over Starlink, and talks in Oslo sent Witkoff on to Moscow.

poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.standing: A Polymarket contract that pays out if Yemen's Houthi movement and Saudi Arabia agree a ceasefire by the end of October. Its price is what traders will stake on a truce, and Gulf oil exports and Red Sea shipping ride on it.
poly-houthi-x-saudi-arabia-effective-cea.recent: The war widened instead. Houthi strikes suspended operations at Riyadh's airport and Qatar Airways halted flights there, missiles killed at least 18 recruits at a Shabwa camp, British Typhoons began intercepting over Saudi Arabia, and a drone hit near the Shaybah oilfield. Riyadh postponed its investor summit to 2027.

stocks:IBM.standing: The century-old American computing company, which earns most of its money from software such as Red Hat and from consulting for large enterprises and governments, and still builds the mainframes many banks run on.

stocks:AVGO.standing: A US chipmaker that designs the custom AI accelerators and networking silicon the largest cloud companies build their data centres on. It also owns VMware, whose software runs much of the world's corporate server estate.

wiki-saudi-arabia.standing: Daily readers of Wikipedia's article on Saudi Arabia, the Gulf kingdom that is the world's largest oil exporter and the guardian of Mecca and Medina. It counts how many people looked the country up, not what happened there.
wiki-saudi-arabia.recent: A Houthi missile hit Riyadh airport twice, killing 13 and wounding over 300, and Qatar Airways suspended flights to Riyadh and Dammam. Allies then moved in: British Typhoons took up patrols to intercept Houthi missiles, Egypt's council approved troops for Saudi Arabia, and Turkey submitted a pact that would bind it to defend Riyadh.
